words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.tr: n. 剥夺国籍；剥夺公民权利；非国有化
words.ex: The law led to the denationalization of many immigrants.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律导致许多移民被剥夺国籍。
words.en: Denationalization refers to the process of transferring ownership of a business, industry, or service from the public sector (government) to the private sector.

words.ex: This superspecies includes many similar bird types.
words.ex_cn: 这个超物种包括许多相似的鸟类类型。
words.en: A superspecies is a group of closely related species that are very similar in morphology and ecology but have not yet fully differentiated into separate species.

words.tr: v. 销声匿迹；突然消失；
words.ex: The magic trick made the coin vanish.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让硬币销声匿迹了。
words.en: If someone or something vanishes, they disappear suddenly or in a way that cannot be explained.

words.ex: The residue left in the cup was sugar.
words.ex_cn: 杯子里留下的残留物是糖。
words.en: A residue of something is a small amount that remains after the main part has gone or been taken or used.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.tr: n. 自我形象；自我印象
words.ex: He has a positive self-image.
words.ex_cn: 他有积极的自我形象。
words.en: The idea that you have of yourself, especially of your abilities, character, and appearance.

words.tr: 短语. 与…不一致；与…有矛盾；与…争吵
words.ex: He is at odds with his brother over money.
words.ex_cn: 他因为钱的问题和他哥哥意见不合。
words.en: In disagreement or conflict with someone or something.

words.tr: v. 承诺；犯（罪、错）；（公开地）表达意见；
words.ex: He commit to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺帮助他的朋友。
words.en: To commit means to carry out or perpetrate a mistake, crime, or immoral act; or to pledge or bind oneself to a certain course of action.

words.tr: phrase. 献身于；致力于；忠于
words.ex: He is committed to learning English every day.
words.ex_cn: 他致力于每天学习英语。
words.en: If you are committed to something, you are willing to give your time and energy to it because you believe in it or because it is important to you.

words.ex: He disconnects the cable from the TV.
words.ex_cn: 他把电缆从电视上拔掉。
words.en: To disconnect something means to separate it from something else to which it is attached or connected.

words.tr: phrase. 多种的；各种各样的
words.ex: He eats a variety of fruits every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天吃各种各样的水果。
words.en: A number or range of things of the same general class that are different or distinct in character or quality.

words.ex: The establishment of the school took five years.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的建立花了五年时间。
words.en: The act of establishing something or the state of being established. It can also refer to an organization or institution, especially a business or public body.

words.ex: The governmental office closed early on Friday.
words.ex_cn: 政府办公室星期五提早关门。
words.en: Relating to the government or the public affairs of a country.

words.tr:
n. 离婚；
v. 和…离婚；
words.ex: They filed for divorce after ten years of marriage.
words.ex_cn: 他们结婚十年后申请了离婚。
words.en: Divorce is the formal ending of a marriage by law.

words.ex: Steve Jobs is the founder of Apple.
words.ex_cn: 史蒂夫·乔布斯是苹果公司的创办者。
words.en: A founder is someone who establishes an organization, company, or institution. As a verb, it means to fail or collapse, especially in terms of a plan or a ship sinking.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.ex: His outlook on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的观点非常积极。
words.en: Your outlook is your general attitude towards life.

words.ex: He erased the wrong answer with an eraser.
words.ex_cn: 他用橡皮擦掉了错误的答案。
words.en: To erase something means to remove it completely from a surface or from a place where it is stored.

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.ex: He is at the forefront of new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他处于新技术的前沿。
words.en: The forefront is the most forward part of something, especially in a literal or metaphorical sense, indicating the leading position in a particular field or activity.

words.tr:
v. 见证；
n. 证人；目击者；
words.ex: He witnessed the accident yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天目睹了那起事故。
words.en: A witness is someone who sees an event happen, especially a crime or an accident. Witnesses are often called upon to give evidence in court.

words.ex: The growth of the plant is slow in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这植物在冬天生长缓慢。
words.en: The process of increasing in physical size, number, value, or strength.

words.ex: The invention of the wheel was a landmark in human history.
words.ex_cn: 轮子的发明是人类历史上的一个里程碑。
words.en: A landmark is a building or feature of a landscape that is easily seen and recognized from a distance, especially one that enables someone to establish their location.

words.ex: The country's economy is growing fast.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的经济正在快速增长。
words.en: The economy of a country or region is the system by which money, industry, and trade are organized.

words.ex: The projection of the movie started at 8 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 电影的放映晚上8点开始。
words.en: A projection is an estimate or forecast of a future situation or trend based on a study of present ones.

words.tr: adj. 人口统计的；人口的；
words.ex: The survey collected demographic data like age and income.
words.ex_cn: 这项调查收集了年龄和收入等人口统计数据。
words.en: Relating to the structure of populations.

words.ex: He will overtake the car ahead soon.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就会超过前面的车。
words.en: If you overtake someone, you go past them because you are moving faster than they are.

words.tr: v. 取代；迫使…离开家园；
words.ex: The new robot will displace the workers on the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 这个新机器人将取代装配线上的工人。
words.en: To displace something or someone means to take their place or to force them to leave their usual place or role.

words.ex: The pendulum swings back and forth in the clock.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆在钟里来回摆动。
words.en: A pendulum is a weight that is hung from a fixed point so that it can swing freely, especially a rod with a weight at the end that regulates the mechanism of a clock.

words.tr: n. 对位法；惬意（或有趣）的对比
words.ex: The composer skillfully used counterpoint to create a complex musical texture.
words.ex_cn: 作曲家巧妙地运用复调手法创造出复杂的音乐织体。
words.en: In music, counterpoint is the relationship between two or more voices that are independent in contour and rhythm, and interdependent in harmony.

words.ex: I can't find my keys here; they must be elsewhere.
words.ex_cn: 我在这儿找不到我的钥匙，它们一定在别处。
words.en: In or to some other place; not here.

words.ex: Unlike his brother, he likes quiet places.
words.ex_cn: 不像他的兄弟，他喜欢安静的地方。
words.en: If one thing is unlike another thing, the two things are different in nature or in appearance.

words.ex: He felt ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对接受这份工作邀约感到矛盾。
words.en: If you say that someone is ambivalent about something, you mean that they have mixed feelings about it or are unsure whether they want it or not.

words.ex: He waved a patriotic flag during the parade.
words.ex_cn: 他在游行中挥舞着一面爱国的旗帜。
words.en: If someone is patriotic, they feel love, loyalty, and respect for their country.

words.ex: He bought equity in a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一家科技公司的股票。
words.en: Equity is the quality of being fair and impartial.

words.tr: phrase. 私募股权；私人股本；私募股权投资（指通过非公开市场投资于非上市公司股权的资本）
words.ex: He works in private equity and helps buy companies.
words.ex_cn: 他从事私募股权工作，帮助收购公司。
words.en: Private equity is a type of investment that involves investing in companies that are not publicly traded on a stock exchange.

words.ex: They make cross-border payments every week.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周进行跨境支付。
words.en: Cross-border refers to something that extends across or beyond the borders of a country, especially involving trade or cooperation between different countries.

words.ex: He can't even walk, let alone run.
words.ex_cn: 他连走都走不了，更别说跑了。
words.en: Used to emphasize the improbability of a contrasting example.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.tr: n. 民族主义；国家主义；
words.ex: Nationalism made people proud of their own country.
words.ex_cn: 民族主义让人们为自己的国家感到自豪。
words.en: Nationalism is a political, social, and economic ideology and movement characterized by the promotion of the interests of a particular nation, especially with the aim of gaining and maintaining the nation's sovereignty over its homeland.

words.ex: The aggregation of raindrops formed a small puddle.
words.ex_cn: 雨滴的聚集形成了一个小水坑。
words.en: An aggregation is a collection or a group of things or people, often gathered together for a particular purpose.

words.ex: Ancient Athens was a city-state.
words.ex_cn: 古雅典是一个城邦。
words.en: A city-state is an independent sovereign city which serves as the center of political, economic, and cultural life over its contiguous territory.

words.ex: His words are a contradiction.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: A contradiction is a situation or statement in which two aspects or elements are opposed to each other, making it impossible for both to be true at the same time.

words.ex: This festival is a regional tradition.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日是一个地区的传统。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a region.

words.tr: n. 米兰人; adj. 米兰的
words.ex: He speaks Milanese at home with his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他回家时和祖父母说米兰方言。
words.en: Relating to Milan or its inhabitants.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.tr: phrase. phr. 找到平衡；权衡取舍
words.ex: He tries to strike a balance between work and family.
words.ex_cn: 他努力在工作和家庭之间取得平衡。
words.en: To achieve a state where different elements are equal or in the correct proportions.

words.tr: phrase. 有充分理由地；合情合理地
words.ex: He left the party with good reason.
words.ex_cn: 他离开派对是有充分理由的。
words.en: If you say that something happened or is true with good reason, you mean that there is a good cause or explanation for it.

words.ex: The columnist writes a weekly opinion piece.
words.ex_cn: 这位专栏作家每周写一篇观点文章。
words.en: A columnist is a journalist who regularly writes a particular kind of article in a newspaper or magazine.

words.tr: adj. 判断错误的；坚持错误的
words.ex: His wrongheaded decision cost the company millions.
words.ex_cn: 他固执的决定让公司损失了数百万。
words.en: If you describe someone as wrongheaded, you mean that although they act in a determined way, their actions and ideas are based on wrong judgments.

words.ex: The herald announced the king's arrival.
words.ex_cn: 传令官宣布了国王的到来。
words.en: A herald is someone who carries or proclaims important news; a forerunner or harbinger.

words.ex: The integration of technology and education improves learning.
words.ex_cn: 技术与教育的结合改善了学习。
words.en: The act or process of combining or adding parts to make a unified whole.

words.tr: n. 清醒；镇定；严肃；节制
words.ex: He values sobriety after his accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后重视清醒。
words.en: The state of being sober, especially in terms of not being under the influence of alcohol.

words.ex: This tradition originates from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统起源于古代。
words.en: To originate means to have a specific beginning or to start something.

words.ex: The company wants to globalize its business.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司想将业务全球化。
words.en: To make something worldwide in scope or application.

words.ex: He has three hobbies, namely reading, swimming, and painting.
words.ex_cn: 他有三个爱好，即阅读、游泳和绘画。
words.en: You use namely to introduce detailed information about the subject you are discussing, or a particular aspect of it.

words.ex: The country supports pluralism in religion and culture.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家支持宗教和文化的多元主义。
words.en: Pluralism is a situation in which people of different social classes, religions, races, etc., are together in a society but continue to have their different traditions and interests.

words.tr: n. 人性；人类；人道；仁慈；
words.ex: Kindness shows the best of humanity.
words.ex_cn: 善良展现了人性中最美好的一面。
words.en: Humanity refers to all human beings collectively or the qualities that make us human, such as kindness, compassion, and the ability to reason.

words.ex: The bridge is stable and safe to cross.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥很稳固，可以安全通过。
words.en: If something is stable, it is not likely to change or come to an end suddenly.

words.tr: phrase. 使逐步淘汰；逐渐停止
words.ex: The company will phase out old machines next year.
words.ex_cn: 公司明年将逐步淘汰旧机器。
words.en: To gradually stop using or providing something, especially over a period of time.

words.ex: The currency in Japan is the yen.
words.ex_cn: 日本的货币是日元。
words.en: The system of money in general use in a particular country.

words.ex: The government gives a subsidy to farmers.
words.ex_cn: 政府向农民提供补贴。
words.en: A subsidy is money that is paid by a government or other authority in order to help an industry or business, or to pay for a public service.

words.ex: After running for an hour, he felt fatigue.
words.ex_cn: 跑了一个小时后，他感到疲乏。
words.en: A feeling of extreme physical or mental tiredness.

words.tr: phrase. 显而易见的；明显的；作为证据的；在场且引人注目的
words.ex: His talent is in evidence during the performance.
words.ex_cn: 他在表演中显而易见地展现了才华。
words.en: If someone or something is in evidence, they are present and can be clearly seen.

words.ex: His participation in the meeting was very important.
words.ex_cn: 他参与会议非常重要。
words.en: The act of taking part in something.

words.tr: n. 代表大会；议会；国会；
words.ex: The congress met to discuss new laws.
words.ex_cn: 代表大会召开以讨论新法律。
words.en: A congress is a formal meeting of representatives, as of various nations, to discuss problems or to make decisions.

words.ex: The stability of the table prevents it from wobbling.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的固定防止它摇晃。
words.en: The state of being stable; the quality of being unchanging.

words.tr: phrase. 就这样吧；顺其自然（表示接受某种不可避免或不愿改变的情况）
words.ex: If you won't change your mind, so be it.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不肯改变主意，那就这样吧。
words.en: Used to express acceptance or resignation to a situation.

words.ex: The new rules add to the cost.
words.ex_cn: 新规定增加了成本。
words.en: To increase or enhance something by adding more to it.

words.tr: n. 意识形态；思想体系；
words.ex: His ideology is based on equality and justice.
words.ex_cn: 他的意识形态基于平等与正义。
words.en: An ideology is a set of beliefs, especially one held by a particular group, that influences the way people think and behave.

words.ex: He uses software to write his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他使用软件写作业。
words.en: Software refers to the programs and other operating information used by a computer.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.ex: He took advantage of the free tickets.
words.ex_cn: 他利用了免费的票。
words.en: To use a particular situation to do or get what you want.

words.ex: Immigration to this country has increased recently.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的移民数量最近增加了。
words.en: Immigration is the act of coming to live permanently in a country that is not your own.

words.ex: The majority of students like pizza.
words.ex_cn: 大多数学生喜欢披萨。
words.en: The majority is the greater number or part of something.

words.ex: The store sells many kinds of textile, like cotton and silk.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售多种纺织品，比如棉和丝绸。
words.en: Textiles are types of cloth or fabric, especially ones that have been woven.

words.tr: phrase. 当然；毫无疑问（表示强烈同意或肯定）
words.ex: You bet I will help you.
words.ex_cn: 当然了，我会帮你。
words.en: Used to express that something is certain or that someone is very willing to do something.

words.ex: The upside of working late is more money.
words.ex_cn: 加班的好处是能赚更多钱。
words.en: The upside is the more positive aspect of a situation that is generally bad.

words.ex: The downside of this job is the long hours.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作的负面是工作时间很长。
words.en: The downside of something is the aspect of it which is less positive, pleasant, or useful than its other aspects.

words.tr: phrase. 使充气；爆炸；发怒；夸大
words.ex: He blew up the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他用嘴把气球吹鼓了。
words.en: If someone blows something up or if it blows up, it is destroyed by an explosion.

words.ex: The deceptive smile hid his true intentions.
words.ex_cn: 那欺骗性的微笑隐藏了他真正的意图。
words.en: If something is deceptive, it encourages you to believe something which is not true.

words.ex: He helped his fellowman in need.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助了有需要的同胞。
words.en: A fellowman refers to another human being, especially one with whom one shares a common humanity or community.

words.ex: He bought a new mirror because of his vanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为虚荣心买了一面新镜子。
words.en: The quality of being vain; excessive pride in or admiration of one's own appearance or achievements.

words.tr: 短语. 就某人而言；在某人这方面
words.ex: For my part, I like pizza.
words.ex_cn: 就我而言，我喜欢披萨。
words.en: Used to indicate that the speaker is expressing their own opinion or perspective on a matter.

words.tr: 短语. 就某人自己而言；在某人自己看来
words.ex: For my own part, I like to read books every night.
words.ex_cn: 就我而言，我喜欢每天晚上读书。
words.en: Used to indicate that the speaker is expressing their own personal opinion or feelings about something.

words.tr: phrase. 作为……的部分；就……而言
words.ex: He is responsible for the part of the project that involves data collection.
words.ex_cn: 他负责项目中涉及数据收集的部分。
words.en: On behalf of or in the interest of a particular person or group.

words.ex: He is capable of solving hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他能解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: If a person or thing is capable of doing something, they have the ability or potential to do it.

words.ex: He gave a definite answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了肯定的答案。
words.en: If something is definite, it is firm and clear, and unlikely to be changed.

words.tr: phrase. 一致的；浑然一体的；同性质的
words.ex: The two sisters are of a piece in their kindness.
words.ex_cn: 这两个姐妹在善良方面是一样的。
words.en: If one thing is of a piece with another, it is consistent with it or similar to it.

words.tr: phrase. 完整的；一致的；连贯的
words.ex: The story is all of a piece, with no contradictions.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事前后一致，没有矛盾。
words.en: Consistent or uniform in nature.

words.tr:
n. 皱纹
v. 起皱纹；弄皱…
words.ex: He has a deep wrinkle on his forehead.
words.ex_cn: 他的额头上有一道深深的皱纹。
words.en: A wrinkle is a small line or fold in something, especially fabric or the skin.

words.ex: The decision was made in accordance with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定是按照规则做出的。
words.en: Agreement or harmony; conformity.

words.ex: He acted in accordance with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他按照规则行事。
words.en: If something is done in accordance with a particular rule or system, it is done in the way that the rule or system says that it should be done.

words.tr: adj. 挚爱的；有深厚感情的；充满深情的
words.ex: She is affectionate with her little brother.
words.ex_cn: 她对弟弟很亲昵。
words.en: If you are affectionate, you show your love or fondness for another person in the way that you behave towards them.

words.ex: His kindliness made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 他的友善让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: The quality of being kind; kindness.

words.ex: The weather is mild today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气温和。
words.en: Mild is used to describe something that is not extreme, severe, or strong, such as weather, taste, or behavior.

words.ex: The scientist created a cocktail of chemicals for the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 科学家为实验配制了一种化学混合物。
words.en: A cocktail is a mixed drink typically made with a combination of alcoholic beverages and other ingredients such as fruit juices, syrups, or cream.

words.ex: The soup is too spicy for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤对我来说太辣了。
words.en: Food that is spicy has a strong, hot flavor.

words.tr: 短语. 有点儿；在某种程度上是
words.ex: He has something of a talent for singing.
words.ex_cn: 他有点唱歌的天赋。
words.en: To some degree; somewhat.

words.ex: Birds fly south by instinct.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类凭本能飞向南方。
words.en: An instinct is the natural tendency that a person or animal has to behave or react in a particular way.

words.ex: We waited in the lounge before our flight.
words.ex_cn: 我们在登机前等在休息室里。
words.en: A lounge is a room in a house or public building where people can sit and relax. As a verb, to lounge means to lie, sit, or stand in a relaxed or lazy way.

words.tr:
v. 嘶嘶地冒泡；发出嘶嘶声
n. 嘶嘶声；气泡；起泡饮料（尤指香槟）
words.ex: The soda began to fizz as soon as it was opened.
words.ex_cn: 苏打水一打开就开始起泡。
words.en: To fizz means to make a hissing or bubbling sound.

words.ex: He sent a remittance to his family last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周给家人汇了一笔款。
words.en: A remittance is a sum of money that you send to someone.

words.tr: adv. 古怪地；怪异地；反常地；
words.ex: He dressed oddly for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着古怪地去参加派对。
words.en: In a manner that is strange or unusual.

words.tr: phrase. 说来也怪；奇怪的是
words.ex: Oddly enough, he likes broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的是，他喜欢西兰花。
words.en: used to say that something is strange or surprising

words.ex: He is the namesake of his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他是他祖父的同名者。
words.en: A namesake is a person or thing that has the same name as another person or thing.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

words.tr:
n. 一小口；
v. 呷；啜；小口喝；
words.ex: He took a sip of water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一小口水。
words.en: To drink something slowly by taking small amounts into your mouth.

words.tr:
n. 小伙子；家伙
v. 皲裂
words.ex: The chap helped me carry the boxes.
words.ex_cn: 那个小伙子帮我搬了箱子。
words.en: A chap is a man or boy. If something chaps your skin, it makes it sore and cracked.

words.ex: In a way, he is right about the problem.
words.ex_cn: 在某种程度上，他对这个问题的看法是正确的。
words.en: To some extent; from a certain point of view.

words.ex: She has curly hair.
words.ex_cn: 她有一头卷发。
words.en: Having curls or a curved shape.

words.tr: phrase. 勉强地；不情愿地；态度恶劣地
words.ex: He accepted the prize with bad grace.
words.ex_cn: 他不情愿地接受了奖品。
words.en: If you do something with bad grace, you do it unwillingly and in a way that shows you are annoyed.

words.ex: He accepted the prize with a bad grace.
words.ex_cn: 他不情愿地接受了奖品。
words.en: If someone does something with a bad grace, they do it unwillingly and in a way that shows they are not happy about it.

words.tr: phrase. 欣然地；优雅地；无怨言地
words.ex: She accepted the loss with good grace.
words.ex_cn: 她坦然接受了失败。
words.en: If you do something with good grace, you do it in a way that shows that you are willing to do it and that you are not annoyed about it.

words.tr: phrase. 欣然地；愉快地；心甘情愿地
words.ex: She accepted the loss with a good grace.
words.ex_cn: 她很好地接受了失败。
words.en: If you do something with a good grace, you do it in a willing and pleasant way, even though you might not really want to do it.

words.tr: n. 中风；划水动作；一击；
words.ex: He had a stroke last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年中风了。
words.en: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain results in cell death. It can also refer to an act of hitting or striking someone or something, or a gentle movement of the hand over a surface.

words.ex: The doctor checked the vein in his arm.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他手臂上的静脉。
words.en: A vein is a tube in your body that carries blood towards your heart. It can also refer to a thin layer of a mineral in rock, or a particular style or mood in writing or speech.

words.ex: The glass is transparent.
words.ex_cn: 这玻璃是透明的。
words.en: If something is transparent, you can see through it.

words.tr: v. 打破；打断；“break”的过去式； adj. 破产的；身无分文的；
words.ex: He broke the glass by accident.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心打碎了玻璃。
words.en: If you are broke, you have no money.

words.tr: phrase. v. 破产；身无分文；没钱了
words.ex: He went broke after buying a new car.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆新车后破产了。
words.en: To become completely without money; to go bankrupt.

words.ex: Hitherto, no one has solved the problem.
words.ex_cn: 迄今为止，没有人解决过这个问题。
words.en: Until now or until the point in time under discussion.

words.tr: phrase. 粘附；坚持；紧跟；忠于
words.ex: The glue will stick the paper to the table.
words.ex_cn: 胶水会把纸粘在桌子上。
words.en: If you stick to a promise, agreement, decision, or principle, you do what you said you would do, or do not change your mind.

words.tr: n. 扑克牌游戏；通条；拨火棍
words.ex: He plays poker with his friends on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他周末和朋友玩扑克。
words.en: Poker is a card game that people play for money, in which they bet on the value of the cards they hold.

words.ex: He always keeps his garden trim and neat.
words.ex_cn: 他总是把花园打理得整洁有序。
words.en: To trim something means to make it tidier or more level by cutting a small amount off it.

words.ex: He left his watch as a pawn at the shop.
words.ex_cn: 他把手表当成了典当品放在店里。
words.en: To pawn something means to leave it with a pawnbroker, who lends you money in exchange. The pawnbroker keeps the item until you pay back the money plus interest.

words.tr: phrase. 穷困潦倒的；失意的；陷入困境的
words.ex: He is down and out after losing his job and home.
words.ex_cn: 他失去工作和家后，一贫如洗。
words.en: If someone is down and out, they have no job, no money, and nowhere to live.

words.tr: phrase. 成碎片；彻底地；完全毁坏地
words.ex: He broke the vase to pieces.
words.ex_cn: 他把花瓶摔得粉碎。
words.en: Completely or thoroughly.

words.tr: phrase. 彻底破碎的；精神或身体极度疲惫的；完全毁坏的
words.ex: The car was all to pieces after the crash.
words.ex_cn: 车祸后，这辆车完全散架了。
words.en: To be extremely upset or in a state of complete disarray.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 情绪崩溃；失去控制；瓦解
words.ex: He goes to pieces when he sees a spider.
words.ex_cn: 他一看到蜘蛛就崩溃了。
words.en: To become so upset or nervous that you cannot control yourself or think clearly.

words.tr: phrase. 彻底崩溃；情绪失控；瓦解
words.ex: He goes all to pieces when he sees a spider.
words.ex_cn: 他一看到蜘蛛就慌了神。
words.en: To become extremely upset or lose control of oneself emotionally.

words.tr: adj. 疯狂的；精神失常的；精神错乱的
words.ex: He thinks it's insane to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 他认为无证驾驶是疯狂的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as insane, you mean that they are very foolish or crazy.

words.tr: n. 微光；隐约的一瞥; adj. 微弱地发光的；薄弱地发光的
words.ex: The glimmering of stars appeared in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中出现了星星的微光。
words.en: A glimmering is a faint, unsteady light or a slight sign or amount of something.

words.tr: phrase. 暗示；意指；想表达的意思
words.ex: I don't understand what you are driving at.
words.ex_cn: 我不明白你到底想说什么。
words.en: If you ask someone what they are driving at, you are asking what they are trying to say or what they are implying.

words.ex: The beacon shines at night to guide ships.
words.ex_cn: 灯塔在夜晚发光以引导船只。
words.en: A beacon is a light or a fire, usually on a hill or tower, which acts as a signal or a warning.

words.ex: The children played near the creek after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在小河旁玩耍。
words.en: A creek is a small, narrow stream or river.

words.tr:
adj. 当前的；流通的；
n. （水、气、电）流；趋势；
words.ex: The current weather is very hot.
words.ex_cn: 当前的天气非常热。
words.en: belonging to the present time; happening or being used or done now

words.ex: He was taken aback by the sudden news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个突如其来的消息时感到吃惊。
words.en: If you are taken aback by something, you are surprised or shocked by it and you cannot respond for a moment.

words.ex: He was taken aback by the sudden news.
words.ex_cn: 他被这个突如其来的消息吓了一跳。
words.en: To be very surprised or shocked by something.

words.tr: phrase. 处于糟糕状态；状况很差；破旧不堪
words.ex: The car is in bad condition.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车状况很差。
words.en: If something is in bad condition, it is not functioning properly or is in a poor state.

words.tr: 状态良好：指物品或人的状态良好，没有损坏或疾病。
words.ex: The car is in good condition.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车状况良好。
words.en: If something is in good condition, it is in a good state or quality, especially because it has been well looked after.

words.tr: phrase. 突然出现；重新露面；调大
words.ex: He didn't turn up to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他没有出席会议。
words.en: To arrive or appear somewhere, often unexpectedly; to increase the volume or intensity of something.

words.ex: He loves to dance to funk music on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在周末随着放克音乐跳舞。
words.en: Funk can refer to a state of fear or depression, or to a style of music that combines elements of rhythm and blues, soul, and jazz.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
words.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties.

words.ex: The dissipation of energy in the system led to a decrease in efficiency.
words.ex_cn: 系统中能量的损耗导致了效率的下降。
words.en: The process by which energy or matter is gradually lost and becomes less concentrated, or the act of wasting money, time, or energy in a careless way.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.ex: He rubs his hands together to warm them.
words.ex_cn: 他搓手来暖和它们。
words.en: To move one's hand or a cloth repeatedly back and forth on the surface of something with firm pressure.

words.ex: There is a vacancy in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 销售部门有一个空缺职位。
words.en: A vacancy is a position or job that is available for someone to fill.

words.tr: phrase. 在某个时候；曾经；迟早
words.ex: At one time or another, everyone makes a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 每个人在某个时候都会犯错。
words.en: Used to indicate that something happened or was true in the past, but not now.

words.tr: phrase. 想出；构思出（主意、计划等）
words.ex: He can think up new ideas very fast.
words.ex_cn: 他能很快想出新点子。
words.en: To invent or devise something.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.ex: His assumption was that the train would be on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是火车会准时。
words.en: An assumption is something that you assume to be the case, even without proof.

words.ex: The mob broke the windows and shouted loudly.
words.ex_cn: 乌合之众砸了窗户并大声喊叫。
words.en: A mob is a large crowd of people, especially one that is disorderly and intent on causing trouble or violence.

words.tr: n. 交叉；相交；十字路口；交叉路口；
words.ex: The intersection of two roads is busy.
words.ex_cn: 两条路的交叉口很繁忙。
words.en: An intersection is a place where roads or other lines meet or cross.

words.ex: The cake has three layers of chocolate.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕有三层巧克力。
words.en: A layer of a substance or material is a quantity or piece of it that covers a surface or that is between two other things.

words.tr: adj. 摇晃的；颤抖的；不稳固的
words.ex: His hands are shaky when he holds the cup.
words.ex_cn: 他拿杯子时手在发抖。
words.en: If you describe a situation as shaky, you mean that it is weak or unstable, and seems unlikely to last long or be successful.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.ex: He bought a bottle of liquor for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对买了一瓶酒。
words.en: Liquor is an alcoholic drink that is made by distillation rather than by fermentation.

words.ex: Before the storm, we decided to stock up on food and water.
words.ex_cn: v. 在风暴来临之前，我们决定储备大量的食物和水。
words.en: To accumulate a large quantity of something for future use.

words.tr: phrase. 用魔法召唤；（魔法般）变出；使浮现脑海
words.ex: The witch tried to conjure up a dragon.
words.ex_cn: 女巫试图用魔法召唤一条龙。
words.en: To make something appear or come to mind, especially as if by magic.

words.ex: He is literally the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他确实是队里最好的球员。
words.en: In a literal manner or sense; exactly.

words.ex: He tried to curb his horse with the reins.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用缰绳勒住马。
words.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

words.ex: We need to get the fire under control quickly.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要迅速把火势控制住。
words.en: To manage to bring something under control, especially something that is difficult to manage or that has been out of control.

words.tr: phrase. 对……作出评价；对……下判断；批评
words.ex: He won't pass judgment on his friend's choice.
words.ex_cn: 他不会对朋友的选择妄加评判。
words.en: To make a decision or form an opinion about someone or something after careful thought.

words.ex: He believed his fate was to become a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自己的命运是成为一名教师。
words.en: Fate is a power that is believed to control what happens in the future.

words.tr: phrase. 给某人一个教训；使某人吸取教训
words.ex: He failed the test, and it taught him a lesson.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，这给他上了一课。
words.en: To make someone realize that they have done something wrong, especially by punishing them or making them suffer in some way.

words.ex: He walks on the sidewalk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在人行道上走路。
words.en: A sidewalk is a path with a hard surface by the side of a road that people walk on.

words.ex: He fractured his arm during the soccer game.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中摔断了手臂。
words.en: If something such as a bone fractures or is fractured, it breaks or cracks.

words.tr: phrase. v. 认真处理；着手应对；正视（问题或现实）
words.ex: He needs to come to grips with his fear of speaking in public.
words.ex_cn: 他需要面对并克服自己对当众讲话的恐惧。
words.en: If you come to grips with a problem or challenge, you start to deal with it or understand it.

words.ex: He gave a sniff of the flower.
words.ex_cn: 他闻了闻那朵花。
words.en: To sniff is to breathe in air through your nose in a way that makes a noise, especially when you are trying to smell something or when you have a cold.

words.ex: Tears begin to well up in her eyes when she hears the sad news.
words.ex_cn: 当她听到这个悲伤的消息时，眼泪开始在她眼中涌出。
words.en: If a liquid wells up, it gradually appears on the surface of something.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 站起来；恢复过来（尤指经历困难后重新振作）
words.ex: After the fall, he tried to get to his feet.
words.ex_cn: 摔倒后，他试图站起来。
words.en: To stand up, especially after sitting or lying down.

words.tr: v. 擦伤；挫伤；出现伤痕；
words.ex: He bruised his knee when he fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来时擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: A bruise is a mark that appears on your skin after you have been injured, but the skin is not broken.

words.ex: He dumped the trash into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他把垃圾倒进了垃圾桶。
words.en: To dump something means to get rid of it quickly and without care, often because it is no longer wanted or needed. It can also refer to the place where waste is left.

words.ex: It was sheer luck that he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛完全是运气。
words.en: Sheer is used to emphasize that a state or situation is complete and does not involve or is not mixed with anything else.

words.tr: v. 淹没；覆盖；压倒；控制；“overwhelm”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The small boat was overwhelmed by the big waves.
words.ex_cn: 小船被巨浪淹没。
words.en: If you are overwhelmed by a feeling or event, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

words.ex: He felt guilt after lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在对朋友撒谎后感到内疚。
words.en: Guilt is an unhappy feeling that you have because you have done something wrong or think that you have done something wrong.

words.ex: He reaches for the book on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他伸手去拿书架上的书。
words.en: To extend out an arm or hand in order to touch or grasp something; to strive to achieve or obtain something.

words.tr: phrase. …得多；尤其；更；到目前为止
words.ex: This is by far the best movie I have seen.
words.ex_cn: 这绝对是我看过的最好的电影。
words.en: By far is used to emphasize that something is the best, worst, biggest, etc., of its kind.

words.tr: adv. 羞怯地；胆怯地；怯懦地
words.ex: He smiled sheepishly after forgetting his lines.
words.ex_cn: 他忘词后尴尬地笑了。
words.en: In a manner that shows embarrassment from shame or a lack of self-confidence.

words.ex: The judge will absolve him of all charges.
words.ex_cn: 法官将免除他所有的罪名。
words.en: If someone is absolved of blame, responsibility, or a sin, they are formally forgiven for it or declared free from it.

words.tr: phrase. 忙碌不停；四处奔波；在路上；在进行中
words.ex: He eats snacks on the go.
words.ex_cn: 他一边赶路一边吃零食。
words.en: If you are on the go, you are very busy and active, moving from one place or task to another.

words.ex: He copes with stress by walking every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天散步来应对压力。
words.en: To cope with a problem or task means to deal with it successfully.

words.ex: He set about cleaning the room after breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完早餐后开始打扫房间。
words.en: To start doing something, especially something that needs a lot of effort or time.

words.ex: He tried to untangle the mess of wires.
words.ex_cn: 他试图理清这堆杂乱的电线。
words.en: To untangle something means to free it from knots or complications, making it straightforward to understand or deal with.

words.ex: The ever-increasing noise makes it hard to sleep.
words.ex_cn: 不断增加的噪音让人难以入睡。
words.en: Continuously becoming greater in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: There are quantities of water in the bottle.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里有大量的水。
words.en: A large amount or number of something.

words.tr: phrase. 大量的；大批的；许多的
words.ex: He bought large quantities of rice for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为聚会买了大量的大米。
words.en: A large amount or number of something.

words.tr: 短语. 大量的，许多的（用于修饰不可数名词）
words.ex: There is a large quantity of water in the lake.
words.ex_cn: 湖里有大量的水。
words.en: A large quantity of refers to a considerable amount or number of something.

words.tr: phrase. （因疾病、饥饿或悲伤）消瘦；逐渐衰弱
words.ex: He will waste away if he keeps eating junk food every day.
words.ex_cn: 如果他每天继续吃垃圾食品，身体会逐渐衰弱。
words.en: To gradually become weaker and thinner, often because of illness or lack of food.

words.tr: v. 奴役；征服；使受控制
words.ex: The cruel king tried to enslave the villagers.
words.ex_cn: 这个残酷的国王试图奴役村民。
words.en: To make someone a slave; to take away someone's freedom.

words.tr:
adj. 令人困惑的；使人糊涂的
v. 使迷惑；使昏乱；“bewilder”的现在分词
words.ex: The maze was bewildering.
words.ex_cn: 这个迷宫令人困惑。
words.en: If something is bewildering, it is very confusing and difficult to understand or to make a decision about.

words.tr: v. 使迷惑；使...不知所措
words.ex: The strange signs bewilder the children.
words.ex_cn: 这些奇怪的符号让孩子们感到迷惑。
words.en: If something bewilders you, it is so confusing or difficult that you cannot understand it.

words.ex: The millennium began in the year 2000.
words.ex_cn: 一千年始于2000年。
words.en: A millennium is a period of one thousand years.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 逐渐消耗，侵蚀（资源、资金等）；对…造成损害
words.ex: The virus can eat into the system and cause damage.
words.ex_cn: 病毒会侵蚀系统并造成损坏。
words.en: To gradually reduce the amount of something, especially money or time, by using it up.

words.ex: He drives a motorcar to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天开车去上班。
words.en: A motorcar is a road vehicle, usually with four wheels, powered by an internal combustion engine or electric motor, and designed to carry a small number of people.

words.ex: The new policy improves worker mobility.
words.ex_cn: 新政策提高了工人的流动性。
words.en: The ability to move or be moved freely and easily.

words.ex: The existence of life on other planets is still unknown.
words.ex_cn: 其他星球上是否存在生命仍不清楚。
words.en: The state or fact of existing; being.

words.ex: Doing homework by hand is time-consuming.
words.ex_cn: 手写作业很耗时。
words.en: If you describe an activity as time-consuming, you mean that it takes a lot of time to do.

words.tr: adj. 横渡大西洋的；大西洋两岸国家的；
words.ex: The transatlantic flight took eight hours.
words.ex_cn: 横渡大西洋的航班花了八个小时。
words.en: Crossing the Atlantic Ocean.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.ex: It is a convention to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是一种习俗。
words.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group, or a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

words.tr:
v. 费力地做；苦干；跋涉
n. 苦工；劳累的工作
words.ex: He toils in the field every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在田里辛苦劳作。
words.en: If you toil, you work very hard doing something that is difficult or tiring.

words.ex: The bacteria multiply quickly.
words.ex_cn: 细菌迅速增加。
words.en: If you multiply one number by another, you add the first number to itself as many times as is indicated by the second number. For example, 2 multiplied by 3 is equal to 6.

words.ex: The mother grooms her puppy every morning.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈每天早上给她的小狗梳理毛发。
words.en: A groom is a man who is getting married. Also, to groom means to clean and brush an animal, or to prepare someone for a particular job or position.

words.tr: n. 便携式电脑；笔记本电脑；
words.ex: He uses a laptop to work from home.
words.ex_cn: 他用笔记本电脑在家工作。
words.en: A laptop is a computer which is small enough to be carried around easily and is designed for use outside an office.

words.tr: n. 综合征；综合症状；典型表现；
words.ex: He was diagnosed with sleep apnea syndrome.
words.ex_cn: 他被诊断出患有睡眠呼吸暂停综合征。
words.en: A syndrome is a set of medical signs and symptoms which are correlated with each other and often associated with a particular disease or disorder.

words.ex: The heavy workload became a burden for her.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量成了她的负担。
words.en: A burden is a heavy load that is difficult to carry, or a duty or responsibility that is hard to bear.

words.ex: He sent the document by fax.
words.ex_cn: 他通过传真发送了文件。
words.en: A fax is a machine that sends and receives documents electronically along a telephone line, or a document that is sent or received using such a machine.

words.ex: He left a voicemail for his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他给老板留了一条语音信箱。
words.en: A system that records and stores telephone messages for later retrieval by the intended recipient.

words.ex: The computer had a small glitch during the presentation.
words.ex_cn: 演示过程中电脑出现了一个小故障。
words.en: A glitch is a small problem or fault that prevents something from working correctly.

words.tr: phrase. 指出通往某事物的道路；指明某事物的方向；为某事物指明方向
words.ex: The stars point the way to the village.
words.ex_cn: 星星指引通往村庄的方向。
words.en: To indicate the direction or method for achieving something.

words.tr: adj. 时间紧迫的；时间紧张的
words.ex: She is time-pressed and can't finish her homework.
words.ex_cn: 她时间紧迫，无法完成作业。
words.en: If you are time-pressed, you have very little time to do something.

words.tr: n. 爆炸；（感情）爆发；激增；
words.ex: The explosion broke all the windows.
words.ex_cn: 爆炸震碎了所有的窗户。
words.en: An explosion is a sudden, violent burst of energy, for example one caused by a bomb.

words.ex: The philosopher wrote a book about life.
words.ex_cn: 这位哲学家写了一本关于生活的书。
words.en: A philosopher is a person who studies or writes about philosophy.

words.ex: A fraction of the students passed the test.
words.ex_cn: 只有一小部分学生通过了考试。
words.en: A fraction is a small part or amount of something.

words.tr: phrase. 大量涌入；源源而来；不断注入
words.ex: People pour in to see the new movie on opening day.
words.ex_cn: 人们在首映日涌入观看新电影。
words.en: If people pour in or pour into a place, they come or go there in large numbers.

words.tr: abbr. 光盘只读存储器；光盘驱动器；“compact disc read-only memory”的缩写
words.ex: He uses a cd-rom to play games.
words.ex_cn: 他用光盘来玩游戏。
words.en: A CD-ROM is a CD on which a very large amount of information can be stored to be read by a computer. CD-ROM is an abbreviation for 'compact disc read-only memory'.

words.ex: Rabbits proliferate quickly in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在野外繁殖得很快。
words.en: If something proliferates, it increases in number or spreads quickly.

words.ex: He won a scholarship to study at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了一项去哈佛学习的奖学金。
words.en: A scholarship is a grant or payment made to support a student's education, awarded on the basis of academic or other achievement.

words.ex: He reads a science journal every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周读一本科学期刊。
words.en: A journal is a newspaper or magazine that deals with a particular subject or professional activity.

words.ex: The publication of his book was delayed.
words.ex_cn: 他的书的出版被推迟了。
words.en: The act of making something available to the public, especially a book, magazine, or newspaper.

words.tr: adj. 荣誉的；名誉的；道义上的
words.ex: He received an honorary degree for his work.
words.ex_cn: 他因自己的工作获得了荣誉学位。
words.en: Given as an honor without the usual requirements or duties.

words.ex: The curator arranged the paintings in the museum.
words.ex_cn: 馆长在博物馆里布置了这些画作。
words.en: A curator is someone who is in charge of the objects or works of art in a museum or art gallery.

words.ex: He loves entomology and collects bugs.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱昆虫学，喜欢收集昆虫。
words.en: The branch of zoology concerned with the study of insects.

words.ex: This is a comparative study of two languages.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个关于两种语言的比较研究。
words.en: You use comparative to show that you are judging something against a previous or different situation. For example, if you say that something is comparative luxury, you mean that it is luxurious compared to something else.

words.ex: He loves zoology and studies animals in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱动物学，研究野外的动物。
words.en: Zoology is the scientific study of animals.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人及时了解某事；让某人跟上某事的最新进展
words.ex: The teacher helps keep the students up with the math lessons.
words.ex_cn: 老师帮助学生跟上数学课程。
words.en: To ensure that someone is informed about or involved in something, especially new developments or changes.

words.tr:
n. 分钟；一会儿；
adj. 微小的；极小的；
words.ex: I waited for five minutes.
words.ex_cn: 我等了五分钟。
words.en: A minute is a unit of time equal to sixty seconds or a sixtieth of an hour.

words.ex: The town is near the frontier of the country.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇靠近国家的边境。
words.en: A frontier is a border between two countries or the area close to it. It can also refer to the limit of knowledge or the most advanced or recent stage in the development of something.

words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使司机系安全带。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc., makes it necessary.

words.tr: phrase. 有义务做某事；不得不做某事
words.ex: I am obliged to finish my homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我必须在晚饭前完成作业。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc. makes it necessary.

words.tr: phrase. 感到有义务做某事；觉得不得不做某事
words.ex: I feel obliged to help my friend.
words.ex_cn: 我觉得有义务帮助我的朋友。
words.en: To feel that you must do something because it is your duty or because someone expects you to do it.

words.ex: He felt discontent with his job.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的工作感到不满。
words.en: Discontent is a feeling of being unhappy because you are not satisfied with your situation or with what you have.

words.ex: He wrote the note in shorthand.
words.ex_cn: 他用速记法写了这条笔记。
words.en: A method of rapid writing by means of abbreviations and symbols, used especially for taking dictation.

words.ex: The signal is received peripherally by the device.
words.ex_cn: 该设备在外围接收信号。
words.en: In a way that is not directly related to the main subject or issue being considered.

words.tr:
n. 预测；预报；
v. 预测；预报；
words.ex: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: If you forecast future events, you say what you think is going to happen in the future.

words.tr: adj. 自己强加的；自愿承担的
words.ex: He made a self-imposed rule to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他给自己定了一条早起的规矩。
words.en: If you describe a restriction or task as self-imposed, you mean that someone has chosen to do it, rather than being forced to do it by someone else.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.ex: He is taking sociology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学里学习社会学。
words.en: Sociology is the study of society, patterns of social relationships, social interaction, and culture that surrounds everyday life.

words.ex: The paint was applied unevenly on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 油漆在墙上涂得不均匀。
words.en: In a way that is not level, smooth, or regular.

words.tr: n. （常用复数）单打比赛；（美）独身者；单程票（single 的复数）; v. 挑出（single...
words.ex: He lives alone as a single man.
words.ex_cn: 他作为一个单身男子独自生活。
words.en: Singles refers to a match or game in sports where one player competes against another, or it can refer to individuals who are not in a romantic relationship.

words.ex: He is an empty-nester who enjoys traveling.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个空巢老人，喜欢旅行。
words.en: An empty-nester is a parent whose children have grown up and left home.

words.tr:
adj. 学龄前的；入学前的；
n. 幼儿园；幼稚园；
words.ex: He attends a preschool program every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上参加学龄前课程。
words.en: A school for children who are too young to attend kindergarten, typically for those aged between three and five.

words.tr:
n. 教养；养育；培育；
v. 培养；
words.ex: Her parents gave her good nurture.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母给了她良好的教养。
words.en: To nurture someone or something is to care for and encourage their growth or development.

words.ex: The dogs had three offspring last spring.
words.ex_cn: 这些狗去年春天生了三只幼崽。
words.en: Someone's offspring are their children.

words.ex: The survey asks about your gender.
words.ex_cn: 这个调查询问你的性别。
words.en: Gender is the state of being male or female, especially when considered with reference to social and cultural differences, not just biological ones.

words.ex: The kitchen has a new washing appliance.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里有一台新的洗衣机。
words.en: An appliance is a device or machine that is used to perform a particular task, especially in the home.

words.tr: adj. 骇人的； v. “appall”的现在分词；
words.ex: The accident caused an appalling sight.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了一幅骇人的景象。
words.en: If you describe something as appalling, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or unpleasant, and that you find it extremely unacceptable.

words.ex: The distribution of students in the class is even.
words.ex_cn: 班级里学生的分布是均匀的。
words.en: The process of giving out or spreading something, or the way in which something is spread or arranged over an area or among a group of people.

words.ex: The village suffered from famine last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄遭受了饥荒。
words.en: A famine is a serious shortage of food in a country, which may cause many people to get sick or die.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.ex: His reaction was quick when the ball came at him.
words.ex_cn: 当球朝他飞来时，他的反应很快。
words.en: Your reaction to something that has happened or something that you have experienced is what you feel, say, or do because of it.

words.ex: A byte stores one letter like 'A'.
words.ex_cn: 一个字节存储一个字母，比如 'A'。
words.en: A byte is a unit of digital information that most commonly consists of eight bits.

words.ex: He waits for the gratification of winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他等待赢得比赛的满足感。
words.en: Gratification is the pleasure or satisfaction you feel when you get something you wanted or worked for.

words.ex: The company streamlined its hiring process.
words.ex_cn: 公司简化了招聘流程。
words.en: To make something such as a business, organization, or process work more effectively by making it simpler or more efficient.

words.tr: n. 公寓的看门人；门房；服务台职员；
words.ex: The concierge helped me carry my bags to the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 公寓的看门人帮我把行李搬到了公寓。
words.en: A concierge is a person who looks after a building, especially a large one such as a hotel or apartment block, and who helps people with their requests.

words.tr: n. 儿童托管；儿童保育；
words.ex: She works in childcare for young children.
words.ex_cn: 她从事幼儿托管工作。
words.en: The care of children, especially by a service or organization.

words.ex: We decorate the room for the party.
words.ex_cn: 我们为派对装饰房间。
words.en: To make something look more attractive by putting things on it or around it.

words.ex: The retailer sells clothes to customers.
words.ex_cn: 这家零售商向顾客出售衣服。
words.en: A retailer is a person or business that sells goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale.

words.ex: He plans to start his retirement next year.
words.ex_cn: 他计划明年退休。
words.en: Retirement is the period of one's life after leaving one's job and ceasing to work.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.ex: There is a shortage of clean water in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄的清洁用水不足。
words.en: A shortage is a situation in which there is not enough of something that is needed.

words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.ex: He crammed the suitcase with clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服塞满了行李箱。
words.en: If you cram things or people into a place, you put them into it even though there is hardly enough room for them.

words.ex: The doctor suggested a natural remedy for the cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议了一种治疗感冒的天然疗法。
words.en: A remedy is a cure or a way of making something better.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.tr: phrase. 就其本质而言；天生地
words.ex: He is by nature a quiet person.
words.ex_cn: 他天性安静。
words.en: If someone has a particular quality by nature, they have it as a natural part of their character.

words.tr: phrase. 关掉；不再想…；不考虑
words.ex: Please switch off the light before you leave.
words.ex_cn: 你离开前请关掉灯。
words.en: To turn off an electrical device by using a switch.

words.ex: He uses his cellphone to call his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他用手机给妈妈打电话。
words.en: A cellphone is a telephone that does not have wires and works by radio, that you can carry with you and use anywhere.

words.tr:
n. 厄运；毁灭；死亡
v. 注定；判决
words.ex: The old prophecy spoke of doom for the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 古老的预言说这个王国将遭遇厄运。
words.en: Doom is a terrible fate or destiny that you cannot avoid, especially death or destruction.

words.tr: adj. 命中注定的； v. 注定；“doom”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The doomed ship sank in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 那艘命中注定的船在风暴中沉没了。
words.en: If something is doomed, it is certain to fail or be destroyed.

words.tr: phrase. 匆忙地；急忙地；在赶时间
words.ex: He is in a rush to catch the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他赶着去赶公交车。
words.en: If you are in a rush, you are trying to do something quickly because you do not have much time.

words.tr: phrase. 赶紧；赶快；匆忙行事
words.ex: Make haste, or we will miss the bus.
words.ex_cn: 快点，否则我们会错过公交车。
words.en: To hurry or move quickly.

words.ex: The file size is reduced by compression.
words.ex_cn: 通过压缩，文件大小被减小了。
words.en: Compression is the act or process of making something smaller or pressing it into a smaller space, or the state of being pressed or squeezed in this way.

words.tr: phrase. 在飞行中；在空中；匆忙地；在活动中
words.ex: The bird is on the wing, flying high above the trees.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿正在飞翔，高高飞过树顶。
words.en: In flight; active or moving about.

words.ex: He works well under pressure.
words.ex_cn: 他在压力下工作得很好。
words.en: Being subjected to stress or coercion.

words.ex: The car's acceleration increased when the driver pressed the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当司机踩油门时，汽车的加速度增加了。
words.en: Acceleration is the rate at which a car or other vehicle can increase its speed, often measured in the time it takes to go from 0 to 60 miles per hour.

words.tr: 短语动词. 严厉管束；发号施令；采取强硬手段控制他人
words.ex: The teacher will crack the whip if students don't follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 如果学生不遵守规则，老师就会严厉管教。
words.en: To take strict control or to enforce discipline in order to make people work harder or more efficiently.

words.ex: The roller coaster gave her a thrill.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让她感到兴奋。
words.en: A thrill is a sudden feeling of great excitement, pleasure, or fear.

words.ex: I like to browse the internet for fun.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢上网浏览消遣。
words.en: To look through or glance at reading matter casually or randomly.

words.tr:
n. 插图说明；标题；字幕
v. 加上说明；加上标题；加上字幕
words.ex: The photo has a caption that says 'Happy birthday'.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片有一个标题，写着‘生日快乐’。
words.en: A caption is a short piece of text under a picture in a book, magazine, or newspaper that describes the picture or explains what is happening in it.

words.ex: He dedicates his time to helping poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他致力于帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: If you dedicate yourself to something, you give all your attention and effort to it.

words.ex: This jacket is waterproof.
words.ex_cn: 这件夹克是防水的。
words.en: Something that is waterproof does not let water pass through it.

words.tr: n. 前景；最显著的位置；
words.ex: The trees in the foreground are very tall.
words.ex_cn: 前景中的树很高。
words.en: The part of a view that is nearest to the observer, especially in a picture or photograph; the most important or prominent position.

words.ex: He moves back and forth between two chairs.
words.ex_cn: 他在两把椅子之间来回移动。
words.en: Moving in one direction and then in the opposite direction repeatedly.

words.ex: The sponge reached saturation and could not hold more water.
words.ex_cn: 海绵达到饱和，再也吸不下更多水了。
words.en: Saturation is the state or process that occurs when no more of something can be absorbed, combined with, or added.

words.tr:
adj. 平行的；
n. 类似的事物；
words.ex: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
words.ex_cn: 这两条线是平行的，永远不会相交。
words.en: Something that is parallel to something else is similar to it in many ways, or happens at the same time as it.

words.ex: He opted to stay home instead of going out.
words.ex_cn: 他选择待在家里而不是出去。
words.en: If you opt for something, or opt to do something, you choose it or decide to do it in preference to anything else.

words.ex: He built his endurance by running every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天早晨跑步来增强耐力。
words.en: The ability to endure an unpleasant or difficult process or situation without giving up.

words.ex: He confesses that he made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承认自己犯了一个错误。
words.en: If you confess to doing something, you admit that you did it.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.tr: n. 社会学家；社会学者；
words.ex: The sociologist studied how people live in cities.
words.ex_cn: 这位社会学家研究了人们在城市中的生活方式。
words.en: A sociologist is someone who studies or is an expert in sociology, which is the study of society and social behavior.

words.ex: He possesses a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有一栋靠近湖边的小房子。
words.en: If you possess something, you have it or own it.

words.ex: No wonder he is tired, he worked all night.
words.ex_cn: 难怪他累了，他整晚都在工作。
words.en: It is not surprising that something is the case.

words.ex: Telecommunications connect people across the world.
words.ex_cn: 电信连接了全世界的人们。
words.en: Telecommunications is the technology of sending signals and messages over long distances using electronic means, such as radio, telephone, television, and the internet.

words.ex: He will run the risk of losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他将面临失去工作的风险。
words.en: To do something that may result in a particular, usually negative, outcome.

words.ex: The temporal change of seasons affects our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 季节的时间变化影响我们的日常生活。
words.en: Relating to time as opposed to eternity; relating to worldly life as opposed to spiritual life.

words.tr: phrasal verb. （物体）倒塌，崩塌；（声音）突然响起
words.ex: The tree will crash down in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 那棵树会在暴风雨中轰然倒下。
words.en: To fall or collapse suddenly and noisily, often with destructive consequences.

words.tr: v. 暂停；中止；延期； suspending
words.ex: The school will suspend the class due to snow.
words.ex_cn: 由于下雪，学校将暂停课程。
words.en: If you suspend something, you delay it or stop it from happening for a while or until a decision is made about it.

words.tr:
n. 贮藏物；隐藏物
v. 贮藏；囤积
words.ex: The treasure hunter found a hoard of gold coins.
words.ex_cn: 寻宝者发现了一堆金币。
words.en: If you hoard things such as food or money, you save or store them, often in secret, because they are valuable or important to you.

words.ex: He took a snapshot of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他拍了一张日落的照片。
words.en: A snapshot is a photograph that is taken quickly and casually, or a brief summary or overview of something.

words.ex: His mood changed after he heard the good news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个好消息后，心情变了。
words.en: A mood is a temporary state of mind or feeling.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.tr: v. 使粉碎；使破碎；使破灭；
words.ex: The stone shattered when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 石头撞到地面时碎裂了。
words.en: If something shatters or is shattered, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.tr:
v. 闷烧；冒烟；郁积
n. 闷烧
words.ex: The fire still smolders in the fireplace.
words.ex_cn: 火还在壁炉里闷烧。
words.en: To burn slowly with smoke but without flame, or to exist in a suppressed state.

words.ex: He believed in his invincibility and never lost a game.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自己不可战胜，从未输过一场比赛。
words.en: The quality of being too powerful to be defeated or overcome.

words.ex: He crumpled the paper in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他把纸揉皱了。
words.en: If you crumple something such as paper or cloth, or if it crumples, it is squashed and becomes full of untidy creases and folds.

words.ex: The ink blot ruined his homework.
words.ex_cn: 墨水污点弄脏了他的作业。
words.en: A blot is a mark or stain that spoils the appearance of something. It can also refer to an act that damages someone's reputation.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 抹去；遮蔽；使遗忘
words.ex: The dark clouds blot out the sun.
words.ex_cn: 乌云遮住了太阳。
words.en: To blot out something means to cover or hide it completely.

words.ex: The ancient city was entombed beneath volcanic ash.
words.ex_cn: 这座古城被火山灰掩埋。
words.en: To place a dead body in a tomb or grave.

words.tr: n. 神风队队员；神风特攻队; adj. 自杀性的；神风特攻队的; n. （日）神风（姓氏）
words.ex: The kamikaze pilots were known for their suicidal missions during World War II.
words.ex_cn: 神风特攻队飞行员在第二次世界大战期间以其自杀式任务而闻名。
words.en: A kamikaze is a Japanese pilot who attacked enemy ships by crashing his aircraft into them during World War II.

words.ex: The room was in chaos after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对之后，房间一片混乱。
words.en: A state of complete disorder and confusion.

words.ex: The meeting was filled with finger-pointing and blame.
words.ex_cn: 会议充满了指责和责难。
words.en: The act of blaming someone or something for a problem or mistake.

words.tr:
n. 报复；报仇
v. 报复
words.ex: He wanted revenge for his brother's death.
words.ex_cn: 他想为他兄弟的死报仇。
words.en: Revenge involves hurting or punishing someone who has hurt or harmed you.

words.tr: phrase. 向……报复；对……进行复仇
words.ex: He wants to take revenge on the man who hurt him.
words.ex_cn: 他想向伤害他的那个人报仇。
words.en: To take revenge on someone means to harm or punish them because they have harmed or offended you.

words.tr: phrase. 对……进行报复；向……复仇
words.ex: He swore to have revenge on his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓要向他的敌人报仇。
words.en: To take action against someone who has harmed you, in order to make them suffer as a result.

words.tr: phrase. 对……进行报复；向……报仇
words.ex: He decided to get revenge on his former boss by exposing the company's illegal activities.
words.ex_cn: 他决定通过揭露公司非法活动来报复他的前老板。
words.en: To take action against someone who has harmed you in order to make them suffer or to punish them.

words.ex: The cop stopped the car for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 警察因超速拦下了那辆车。
words.en: A cop is a police officer. To cop means to catch or arrest someone.

words.ex: The commentator explained the game clearly.
words.ex_cn: 评论员清晰地解释了比赛。
words.en: A commentator is someone who gives a commentary on something such as a sports event or a television program.

words.tr: adj. 悲剧的；悲惨的；不幸的；
words.ex: The accident was a tragic event.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故是一场悲剧。
words.en: A tragic event or situation is extremely sad, usually because it involves death or suffering.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.ex: The police caught the culprit who stole the bike.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了偷自行车的罪犯。
words.en: A culprit is someone who has done something wrong or illegal.

words.ex: The birds flew home at dusk.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黄昏时飞回家。
words.en: Dusk is the time just before night when the daylight has almost gone but when it is not completely dark.

words.ex: I often think back on my childhood with great fondness.
words.ex_cn: v. 我经常非常怀念地回想我的童年。
words.en: To recall or remember something from the past.

words.tr: phrase. 回忆起；回想（某事或某时）
words.ex: I often think back to my childhood with great fondness.
words.ex_cn: 我经常怀着极大的喜爱回忆起我的童年。
words.en: To remember or recall something from the past.

words.ex: She wears a necklace made of crystal.
words.ex_cn: 她戴一条水晶制成的项链。
words.en: A crystal is a solid that has a regular, repeating arrangement of atoms. Crystals are often transparent and can be used in jewelry or as decorative objects.

words.ex: He explained the plan in detail.
words.ex_cn: 他详细地解释了这个计划。
words.en: Including all the facts or aspects of a situation.

words.tr: phrase. 非常详细地；极其详尽地
words.ex: He explained the plan in great detail.
words.ex_cn: 他详细地解释了这个计划。
words.en: With thorough and comprehensive attention to all aspects.

words.tr: phrase. 以极其清晰透彻的细节；如水晶般清晰详尽地
words.ex: The report described the accident in crystal detail.
words.ex_cn: 报告中非常详细地描述了这起事故。
words.en: With exceptionally clear and vivid precision.

words.ex: The aftermath of the storm left many trees down.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，许多树被吹倒了。
words.en: The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it.

words.tr: phrase. 在……之后；在……的余波中；在……的后续阶段
words.ex: In the aftermath of the storm, the town cleaned up the broken trees.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，小镇清理了倒下的树木。
words.en: During the period following a significant event, especially a disaster.

words.ex: The storm left only wreckage on the beach.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在海滩上只留下了残骸。
words.en: The remains of something that has been badly damaged or destroyed.

words.ex: The children played on the rubble after the building fell.
words.ex_cn: 建筑物倒塌后，孩子们在碎石上玩耍。
words.en: Rubble is the broken pieces of stone, brick, etc., that are left when a building falls down or is destroyed.

words.tr:
v. 摘；拔；猛拉；拨弹
n. 胆识；胆量；快而猛地拉
words.ex: He plucked a flower from the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他从花园里摘了一朵花。
words.en: To pluck means to pull something quickly to remove it or to play a musical instrument by pulling the strings with your fingers. As a noun, it refers to the quality of being brave and determined.

words.ex: The note on the fridge is a reminder to buy milk.
words.ex_cn: 冰箱上的便条是提醒买牛奶的东西。
words.en: A reminder is something that makes you think about or remember someone or something else.

words.ex: The storm left debris on the road.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在道路上留下了碎片。
words.en: The remains of something that has been destroyed or broken up.

words.tr:
n. 树液；
v. 使逐渐耗竭；使削弱；
words.ex: The tree releases sap in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在春天流出树液。
words.en: Sap is the watery fluid that circulates in the vascular system of a plant, carrying nutrients and sugars. It can also refer to the vitality or energy of a person or thing.

words.tr:
adj. 爆炸的；
n. 炸药；
words.ex: The explosive material was handled with care.
words.ex_cn: 爆炸性材料被小心地处理。
words.en: An explosive substance is capable of causing an explosion. It can also refer to something that is likely to cause an outburst or a sudden increase in activity or emotion.

words.ex: His sudden win in the race was a real coup.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中突然获胜，真是了不起的成就。
words.en: A coup is a sudden, violent, and illegal seizure of power from a government.

words.tr: adj. 武装的； v. “arm”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The armed soldiers marched through the town.
words.ex_cn: 武装的士兵穿过城镇。
words.en: Equipped with weapons, especially firearms.

words.tr: n. 卫兵；（英）禁卫军官兵；（美）国民警卫队士兵
words.ex: The guardsman stood at attention, ready to protect the palace.
words.ex_cn: 卫兵立正站好，准备保护宫殿。
words.en: A guardsman is a soldier who is a member of a guard, especially one who guards a royal or important person.

words.ex: He wears a helmet when he rides a bike.
words.ex_cn: 他骑自行车时戴头盔。
words.en: A helmet is a strong, hard hat which is worn to protect your head.

words.ex: The soldier wore camouflage to hide in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿着伪装服在森林中隐藏自己。
words.en: Camouflage is the way in which some animals are colored and shaped so that they cannot easily be seen in their natural surroundings.

words.tr:
n. 隆隆声；辘辘声
v. 隆隆作响；辘辘行驶
words.ex: The dog let out a low rumble.
words.ex_cn: 狗发出了一声低沉的咆哮。
words.en: To make a continuous deep, resonant sound; to speak in a low, deep voice.

words.tr:
n. 护送；护航；护卫
v. 护航；护送
words.ex: The army sent a convoy to protect the trucks.
words.ex_cn: 军队派出护送队保护卡车。
words.en: A convoy is a group of vehicles or ships traveling together, typically accompanied by armed troops, warships, or other vehicles for protection.

words.tr: phrase. 以护航/护送队形式；结队行驶；在护送下
words.ex: The trucks moved in convoy through the desert.
words.ex_cn: 卡车车队在沙漠中行进。
words.en: Traveling together in a group, typically for protection or efficiency.

words.ex: He bought a magazine at the newsstand.
words.ex_cn: 他在报摊上买了一本杂志。
words.en: A newsstand is a place where newspapers and magazines are sold, often located on the street or in a public area.

words.ex: The detective spent hours in the morgue examining the body.
words.ex_cn: 侦探在陈尸所花了几个小时检查尸体。
words.en: A morgue is a building or a room in a hospital where dead bodies are kept before they are buried or cremated.

words.ex: The nerve in his finger was damaged.
words.ex_cn: 他手指里的神经受到了损伤。
words.en: A nerve is a bundle of fibers that transmits impulses of sensation to the brain or spinal cord, and impulses from these to the muscles and organs. It also refers to the courage or control needed to do something difficult or dangerous.

words.tr: phrase. 神经中枢；控制中心
words.ex: The city hall is the nerve center of local government.
words.ex_cn: 市政厅是地方政府的中心。
words.en: The nerve center is the most important part of an organization or system, where the main activities are controlled.

words.ex: France was an ally of the United States in the war.
words.ex_cn: 法国在战争中是美国的同盟者。
words.en: An ally is a country, organization, or person that helps and supports another country, organization, or person in a difficult situation.

words.ex: The workers showed solidarity during the strike.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在罢工期间表现出团结。
words.en: Solidarity is unity or agreement of feeling or action, especially among individuals with a common interest; mutual support within a group.

words.ex: The investigator asked the witness a few simple questions.
words.ex_cn: 调查员问了证人几个简单的问题。
words.en: An investigator is someone whose job is to investigate a crime, accident, or other matter.

words.ex: The bomber flew over the city at night.
words.ex_cn: 轰炸机在夜间飞越了这座城市。
words.en: A bomber is a military aircraft designed to carry and drop bombs.

words.ex: He was arrested as an accomplice to the robbery.
words.ex_cn: 他因作为抢劫的帮凶而被逮捕。
words.en: An accomplice is someone who helps another person to commit a crime.

words.tr:
adj. 狂热入迷的；盲信的
n. 狂热者；盲信者
words.ex: He is a fanatic fan of soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他对足球狂热入迷。
words.en: A fanatic is a person who is very enthusiastic about and devoted to a particular activity, cause, or belief, often to an extreme degree.

words.tr: phrase. 早在某事之前；远在某事发生之前
words.ex: She had heard the story long before something was mentioned.
words.ex_cn: 她很久以前就听说过这个故事，远在提到某事之前。
words.en: A considerable period of time prior to a specific event or time.

words.tr: phrase. 在…很久之后；远远晚于某事
words.ex: He still thinks about her long after they broke up.
words.ex_cn: 他们分手很久后，他仍然会想起她。
words.en: A considerable time after a particular event or point in time.

words.ex: The new policy will bring down prices.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将降低价格。
words.en: To cause something to fall or collapse; to reduce the level or amount of something; to cause someone in a position of power to lose their position.

words.ex: He felt deep grief after his dog died.
words.ex_cn: 他的狗去世后，他感到深深的悲痛。
words.en: Intense sorrow, especially caused by someone's death.

words.ex: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
words.ex_cn: 地球围绕太阳转。
words.en: If something revolves or if you revolve something, it moves or turns around a central point or line.

words.tr:
adj. 清楚的；明确的；清晰的；清澈的；晴朗的；
v. 清空；清除；放晴；使明确；
adv. 清楚地；彻底地；
words.ex: The instructions are clear.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很清楚。
words.en: Free from anything that marks or darkens; transparent; bright; not obscure or ambiguous; easily understood; free from guilt or blame.

words.ex: She mourns her dog every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天都在哀悼她的狗。
words.en: To feel or express deep sorrow or regret for someone or something.

words.ex: The flowers will perish if you don't water them.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不给花浇水，它们会死。
words.en: If people or animals perish, they die as a result of very harsh conditions or as the result of an accident.

words.ex: They placed a memorial at the site of the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他们在事故地点放置了一座纪念物。
words.en: A memorial is a structure or event established to remind people of a person or event.

words.tr:
v. 目瞪口呆地看；裂开
n. 目瞪口呆地看；裂口
words.ex: The children gape at the magic show.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们张大嘴看着魔术表演。
words.en: To open the mouth wide; to stare with open mouth, as in wonder.

words.ex: A sliver of wood stuck in his finger.
words.ex_cn: 一小片木头扎进了他的手指。
words.en: A sliver is a small, thin piece of something that has been cut, broken, or torn off from a larger piece.

words.ex: The hummingbird flies quickly around the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜂鸟快速地在花朵周围飞翔。
words.en: A very small, brightly coloured bird with a long thin beak, whose wings move very fast and make a humming sound.

words.tr: phrase. 在…的时间之内；在…的期间内
words.ex: She completed the project in the space of a week.
words.ex_cn: 她在一周的时间内完成了项目。
words.en: Within the duration of; in the time it takes to do something.

words.tr: 介词短语. 在……的时间或空间范围内；在……期间或跨度内
words.ex: He finished the job within the space of an hour.
words.ex_cn: 他在一小时内完成了工作。
words.en: Within the duration or scope of a particular period or area.

words.tr: v. 重击；猛击；突然深有感触
words.ex: The knight will smite the dragon with his sword.
words.ex_cn: 骑士将用他的剑击打龙。
words.en: To strike or hit someone or something very hard.

words.tr: phrase. 接替某人的位置或角色，承担某人的职责
words.ex: It's not easy to fill sb.'s shoes when they've been in the role for so long.
words.ex_cn: 在一个角色中待了这么久之后，接替某人的位置并不容易。
words.en: To take someone's place and do their job or role as well as they did.

words.tr: phrase. 设身处地为某人着想；接替某人的职位或责任
words.ex: It's hard to step into someone else's shoes and understand their perspective.
words.ex_cn: 很难代替别人的位置并理解他们的观点。
words.en: To take over someone's responsibilities or position.

words.tr: n. 孤儿；失去生母的幼小动物
words.ex: The boy lives with his uncle because he is an orphan.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩和叔叔住在一起，因为他是个孤儿。
words.en: An orphan is a child whose parents are dead.

words.tr:
v. 神气十足地走；大摇大摆地走
n. 大摇大摆；神气十足
words.ex: He walks with swagger down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他大摇大摆地走在街上。
words.en: If someone swaggers, they walk in a very proud and confident way, often in a way that annoys other people.

words.ex: The memory of her smile is indelible.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的记忆是无法磨灭的。
words.en: If you say that something leaves an indelible impression, you mean that it is very unlikely to be forgotten.

words.ex: The war caused terrible carnage on both sides.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争在双方都造成了惨烈的大屠杀。
words.en: The killing of a large number of people, especially in a violent way.

words.ex: She wore a necklace made of amber.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一条琥珀制成的项链。
words.en: Amber is a hard, translucent, yellowish-brown substance that is used for making jewelry or other objects. It is formed from the resin of ancient trees.

words.ex: He checks the calendar every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都看日历。
words.en: A calendar is a chart or device which displays the date and the day of the week, and often the whole of a particular year divided up into months, weeks, and days.

words.ex: We will revisit the beach next summer.
words.ex_cn: 我们明年夏天会重游那片海滩。
words.en: If you revisit a place, you return there for a second or subsequent time, often after a considerable period.

words.tr: phrase. 挑挑拣拣地吃；不断挑剔；反复抠弄；轻轻拉扯
words.ex: He picks at his food when he is not hungry.
words.ex_cn: 他不饿的时候会挑食。
words.en: To criticize or find fault with someone or something in a petty way; to eat very little or without enthusiasm.

words.tr:
n. 痂；疥癣；拒罢工的工人
v. 结疤；当工贼
words.ex: The wound healed and a scab formed.
words.ex_cn: 伤口愈合了，结了痂。
words.en: A scab is a hard, dry covering that forms over a wound or sore as it heals. It can also refer to a person who continues working while others are on strike, often viewed negatively by the strikers.

words.ex: The wound will heal in a few days.
words.ex_cn: 伤口几天后就会愈合。
words.en: To make or become healthy or whole again; to cure or recover from an injury or illness.

words.tr: v. 倾倒；摇摇欲坠；将…推翻；使…跌倒
words.ex: The strong wind toppled the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 大风把那棵老树吹倒了。
words.en: If someone or something topples, or if someone or something topples them, they become unsteady or unstable and fall over.

words.tr:
n. 外衣；大衣；
v. 覆盖；
words.ex: He put on his coat before going out.
words.ex_cn: 他出门前穿上了外衣。
words.en: A coat is a piece of clothing with long sleeves which you wear over your other clothes when you go outside.

words.ex: She tied the box with a thin string.
words.ex_cn: 她用一根细线把盒子绑了起来。
words.en: A string is a thin piece of rope or cord, or a series of things connected together.

words.tr: adj. 心碎的；伤心的；极度沮丧的
words.ex: She was brokenhearted after the breakup.
words.ex_cn: 分手后她伤心欲绝。
words.en: If someone is brokenhearted, they are extremely sad about something that has happened to them.

words.ex: He said farewell to his friends before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前向朋友们道别。
words.en: Farewell is an expression of good wishes at parting, often used to say goodbye.

words.tr:
v. 旋动；（使）成漩涡；盘旋
n. 漩涡；涡状形
words.ex: The milk swirls in the coffee.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶在咖啡里旋转。
words.en: If something swirls or if you swirl it, it moves around and around quickly.

words.tr: n. 托钵僧; 像托钵僧似的人
words.ex: The dervish spun around in a trance-like state.
words.ex_cn: 托钵僧处于恍惚状态中旋转。
